ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, when the input terminals A = 1, B = 0, and C = 0, the logical state of the output terminal F is __.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, looking at the circuit from left to right, input terminals A and B are respectively connected to an upper logic block marked “≥1”; input terminal C is connected to a lower logic block marked “1”, and the output terminal of this lower logic block has a small circle, indicating an inverted output. The output of the upper logic block and the output after inversion below together enter the final “≥1” logic block on the right; there is also a small circle before F at the output terminal of the final logic block, indicating that the final output is inverted again. Reasoning: Given by the problem, A=1, B=0, C=0. The upper “≥1” block is equivalent to an OR condition, so A OR B = 1 OR 0 = 1. Even if the lower C branch is treated as inversion according to the small circle at the output, one input of the final “≥1” gate is already provided as 1 by the upper branch, therefore the output of the final “≥1” gate before inversion is 1. The small circle at the final output terminal inverts this 1, so F=0.

method.method_draft: First describe the visual circuit left to right: A and B feed an OR-type block marked ≥1; C feeds a lower block with an output bubble; both resulting signals feed a final ≥1 block whose output also has a bubble before F. From the text, substitute A=1, B=0, C=0. Compute the upper signal as A OR B = 1 OR 0 = 1. The lower branch may be evaluated using the shown bubble as the inverted C branch, but regardless the final ≥1 gate receives at least one 1 because the upper branch is 1. Therefore the final OR output before the bubble is 1, and the output bubble inverts it, giving F=0.
